questions.s: The number of moles in 36 g of water (H₂O) is
questions.e: Molar mass of H₂O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol, so n = 36/18 = 2.0 mol. Using 36 as the molar mass would give 1.0 mol.

questions.s: The number of molecules in 0.5 mol of carbon dioxide is
questions.e: N = n × Nₐ = 0.5 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.01 × 10²³ molecules. 6.02 × 10²³ is the number in a full mole.

questions.s: The molar mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃ (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16), is
questions.e: 40 + 12 + 3(16) = 100 g/mol. 84 results from counting only two oxygen atoms.

questions.s: A compound contains 40.0 % carbon, 6.7 % hydrogen and 53.3 % oxygen by mass. Its empirical formula is
questions.e: Moles: C 40.0/12 = 3.33, H 6.7/1 = 6.7, O 53.3/16 = 3.33. Dividing by 3.33 gives 1 : 2 : 1, so CH₂O. C₂H₄O would need a different mass ratio.

questions.s: The volume occupied at STP by 8 g of oxygen gas (O₂ = 32 g/mol) is
questions.e: n = 8/32 = 0.25 mol, and V = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 dm³. 11.2 dm³ would be the volume of 16 g.

questions.s: Carbon burns completely: C + O₂ → CO₂. The mass of carbon dioxide formed from 6 g of carbon is
questions.e: 6 g of carbon is 6/12 = 0.5 mol, which gives 0.5 mol of CO₂ = 0.5 × 44 = 22 g. 44 g is the mass from a whole mole of carbon.

questions.s: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 2 g of hydrogen are mixed with 16 g of oxygen. The mass of water formed is
questions.e: H₂ is 1 mol and O₂ is 0.5 mol. 1 mol of H₂ needs 0.5 mol of O₂, so both are used up and 1 mol of water = 18 g forms. 20 g is the sum 2 + 16 + 2, which is meaningless.

questions.s: A reaction should give 24 g of product in theory but gives 18 g in practice. The percentage yield is
questions.e: Percentage yield = actual/theoretical × 100 = 18/24 × 100 = 75 %. 133 % comes from inverting the ratio.

questions.s: The number of neutrons in an atom of ²³₁₁Na is
questions.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12. 11 is the number of protons.

questions.s: The number of electrons in an Fe³⁺ ion (atomic number of Fe = 26) is
questions.e: A neutral iron atom has 26 electrons; the 3+ ion has lost three, leaving 23. Adding three would give 29.

questions.s: Which ion is isoelectronic with an argon atom?
questions.e: Argon has 18 electrons, and K⁺ has 19 − 1 = 18. Na⁺ and O²⁻ each have 10 electrons, and Br⁻ has 36.

questions.s: The ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is
questions.e: A half-filled d subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron moves to 3d, giving 3d⁵ 4s¹. The expected 3d⁴ 4s² is the common wrong answer.

questions.s: The maximum number of electrons that can occupy the shell with n = 3 is
questions.e: The capacity is 2n² = 2 × 9 = 18. 8 is the capacity of the second shell and 32 that of the fourth.

questions.s: The total number of orbitals in the shell with n = 3 is
questions.e: The number of orbitals is n² = 9 (one 3s, three 3p and five 3d). 18 is the number of electrons, not orbitals.

questions.s: Which set of quantum numbers (n, l, m) is NOT permitted?
questions.e: The value of l must be less than n, ranging from 0 to n − 1. For n = 2, l can only be 0 or 1, so l = 2 is impossible.

questions.s: According to Hund's rule, electrons in a set of degenerate orbitals
o: occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins first
pair up in the lowest-energy orbital before moving on
always have opposite spins within a subshell
fill the orbitals of highest energy before the rest
questions.e: Hund's rule minimises repulsion: each degenerate orbital gets one electron (same spin) before any is doubly occupied. Pairing first is the opposite of the rule.

questions.s: The Pauli exclusion principle states that
o: electrons fill the lowest energy orbitals first
no two electrons in an atom can have the same four quantum numbers
the position and momentum of an electron cannot both be known exactly
degenerate orbitals fill singly before pairing
questions.e: Two electrons in one orbital must therefore differ in spin. The other statements are the Aufbau principle, the uncertainty principle and Hund's rule.

questions.s: The Balmer series in the hydrogen emission spectrum lies mainly in the
questions.e: Balmer lines arise from transitions down to n = 2 and four of them are visible. Transitions to n = 1 (Lyman) are ultraviolet, and to n = 3 (Paschen) infrared.

questions.s: According to Bohr's theory, the energy of the electron in the n = 2 level of a hydrogen atom is
questions.e: Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV, so E₂ = −13.6/4 = −3.4 eV. −13.6 eV is the ground state and −1.51 eV is n = 3.

questions.s: The first line of the Balmer series arises from the electron transition
questions.e: The Balmer series ends at n = 2, and the first (longest-wavelength) line starts from the nearest level, n = 3. Option n = 2 to n = 1 is the first Lyman line.

questions.s: Boyle's law states that, for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature,
o: pressure is inversely proportional to volume
pressure is directly proportional to volume
volume is directly proportional to temperature
pressure is directly proportional to temperature
questions.e: At constant temperature PV = constant, so pressure falls as volume rises. The other two options are the Charles' law and Gay-Lussac's law relations.

questions.s: A gas at 2 atm occupies 3 dm³. At constant temperature it is compressed to 1 dm³. The new pressure is
questions.e: P₂ = P₁V₁/V₂ = 2 × 3/1 = 6 atm. 0.67 atm results from inverting the volume ratio.

questions.s: A gas occupies 2.0 dm³ at 300 K. At constant pressure it is heated to 450 K. The new volume is
questions.e: V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 2.0 × 450/300 = 3.0 dm³. 1.3 dm³ comes from inverting the temperature ratio.

questions.s: The density of oxygen gas at STP (O₂ = 32 g/mol, molar volume 22.4 dm³) is about
questions.e: Density = molar mass/molar volume = 32/22.4 = 1.43 g/dm³. 0.70 g/dm³ is 22.4/32, the inverted ratio.

questions.s: The rates of effusion of hydrogen (2 g/mol) and methane (16 g/mol) under the same conditions are in the ratio H₂ : CH₄ of
questions.e: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(16/2) = √8 ≈ 2.8. 8 : 1 forgets the square root.

questions.s: A mixture contains 1 mol of hydrogen and 3 mol of helium at a total pressure of 2 atm. The partial pressure of hydrogen is
questions.e: Mole fraction of H₂ = 1/4, so partial pressure = 0.25 × 2 = 0.5 atm. 1.5 atm is the partial pressure of helium.

questions.s: Taking R = 0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, the number of moles of gas in 2 dm³ at 3 atm and 27 °C is about
questions.e: n = PV/RT = (3 × 2)/(0.0821 × 300) = 0.244 mol, with T converted to kelvin. Using 27 instead of 300 for T would give a far larger answer, and 0.49 mol doubles the volume.

questions.s: Among the following gases, the one that behaves most nearly as an ideal gas at ordinary conditions is
questions.e: Helium atoms are small, non-polar and have very weak attractions. NH₃, CO₂ and Cl₂ have stronger intermolecular forces and larger deviations.

questions.s: In the van der Waals equation, the constant 'a' corrects for
o: the finite volume of the molecules themselves
the temperature of the gas sample
the number of moles of gas present
questions.e: The term a(n/V)² reduces the pressure term because molecules attract each other. The finite volume of molecules is corrected by 'b'.

questions.s: A liquid boils when its
o: density equals the density of its vapour
questions.e: At the boiling point bubbles of vapour can form because the vapour pressure matches the surrounding pressure. That is why water boils at a lower temperature on a mountain.

questions.s: Which of the following is a covalent network solid?
questions.e: In diamond every carbon is bonded to four others in one giant lattice, giving a very high melting point. NaCl is ionic, and CO₂ and ice are molecular solids.

questions.s: Graphite conducts electricity because
o: it contains free ions between the layers
all four valence electrons of carbon are free
its layers are joined by strong covalent bonds
one electron per carbon is delocalised in each layer
questions.e: Each carbon is bonded to three others, and its fourth electron moves freely along the sheet. Graphite has no ions, and the weak forces between layers do not carry current.

questions.s: The number of atoms per unit cell in a face-centred cubic lattice is
questions.e: 8 corner atoms × 1/8 + 6 face atoms × 1/2 = 1 + 3 = 4. A body-centred cubic cell holds 2 atoms.

questions.s: The number of oxygen atoms in 11.2 dm³ of oxygen gas at STP is
questions.e: 11.2 dm³ is 0.5 mol of O₂, which contains 1 mol of atoms = 6.02 × 10²³. 3.01 × 10²³ counts molecules instead of atoms.

questions.s: The mass of 3.01 × 10²² molecules of ammonia (N = 14, H = 1) is
questions.e: n = 3.01 × 10²²/6.02 × 10²³ = 0.05 mol, and mass = 0.05 × 17 = 0.85 g. 8.5 g is a power-of-ten error.

questions.s: The percentage of nitrogen by mass in ammonium sulphate, (NH₄)₂SO₄ (N = 14, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16), is
questions.e: M = 2(14 + 4) + 32 + 64 = 132, and N is 28/132 = 21.2 %. 10.6 % counts only one nitrogen.

questions.s: Calcium carbonate decomposes: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. A 250 g sample that is 80 % pure CaCO₃ gives what mass of CaO (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)?
questions.e: Pure CaCO₃ = 0.8 × 250 = 200 g = 2 mol, giving 2 mol of CaO = 2 × 56 = 112 g. 140 g ignores the impurity.

questions.s: The percentage by mass of water in CuSO₄·5H₂O (Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1) is
questions.e: M = 159.5 + 90 = 249.5, and 90/249.5 × 100 = 36.1 %. 63.9 % is the percentage of anhydrous CuSO₄.

questions.s: Chlorine has two isotopes, ³⁵Cl (75 %) and ³⁷Cl (25 %). Its average atomic mass is
questions.e: 0.75 × 35 + 0.25 × 37 = 26.25 + 9.25 = 35.5. A simple mean of 35 and 37 would wrongly give 36.0.

questions.s: Rutherford's gold-foil experiment showed that most alpha particles passed straight through because the atom
questions.e: Only a few particles were deflected, by the tiny dense nucleus. A uniform positive sphere (Thomson's model) would deflect none strongly.

questions.s: The mass of 0.25 mol of sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃ (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16), is
questions.e: M = 46 + 12 + 48 = 106 g/mol, so mass = 0.25 × 106 = 26.5 g. 106 g is the mass of a full mole.

questions.s: The number of moles in 5.6 dm³ of nitrogen gas at STP is
questions.e: n = 5.6/22.4 = 0.25 mol. 0.5 mol would need 11.2 dm³.

questions.s: A hydrocarbon contains 85.7 % carbon and 14.3 % hydrogen by mass and has a molar mass of 56 g/mol. Its molecular formula is
questions.e: C : H = 85.7/12 : 14.3/1 = 7.14 : 14.3 = 1 : 2, so the empirical formula is CH₂ (mass 14). 56/14 = 4, giving C₄H₈.

questions.s: The ground-state electronic configuration of copper (Z = 29) is
questions.e: A completely filled 3d subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron moves into 3d. The expected 3d⁹ 4s² is the common wrong answer.

questions.s: The maximum number of electrons that can occupy the shell with n = 4 is
questions.e: The capacity is 2n² = 2 × 16 = 32. 18 is the capacity of n = 3.

questions.s: A gas at 1.0 atm and 300 K is in a rigid container. If it is heated to 600 K, its pressure becomes
questions.e: At constant volume P ∝ T (in kelvin), so P doubles to 2.0 atm. 0.5 atm results from inverting the ratio.

questions.s: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. The volume of hydrogen at STP from 6.5 g of zinc (Zn = 65) is
questions.e: 6.5/65 = 0.1 mol of Zn gives 0.1 mol of H₂, and 0.1 × 22.4 = 2.24 dm³.

questions.s: A student obtains 20 g of a product when the theoretical yield is 25 g. The percentage yield is
questions.e: Percentage yield = 20/25 × 100 = 80 %. 125 % inverts the ratio.

questions.s: After the 4s subshell, the next subshell to be filled in the Aufbau order is
questions.e: By the n + l rule, 3d (n + l = 5) is lower than 4p (n + l = 5, but higher n), so 3d fills first. 4p comes after 3d, and 4d and 5s are higher still.

questions.s: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but molten sodium chloride does, because in the molten state
o: the ions are free to move
questions.e: In the solid, ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice. On melting they move and carry the current.

questions.s: Which of the following molecules contains a triple bond?
questions.e: Each nitrogen atom needs three more electrons, so two nitrogen atoms share three pairs. O₂ has a double bond, and Cl₂ and H₂ have single bonds.

questions.s: The shape of the ammonia molecule, NH₃, is
questions.e: Nitrogen has three bond pairs and one lone pair, so four electron pairs are arranged tetrahedrally but the atoms form a pyramid. Trigonal planar would need no lone pair.

questions.s: The H–O–H bond angle in a water molecule is approximately
questions.e: Water has two bond pairs and two lone pairs, and the stronger lone-pair repulsion squeezes the angle below the tetrahedral 109.5°. 107° is the angle in NH₃.

questions.s: The shape of the boron trifluoride molecule, BF₃, is
questions.e: Boron has three bond pairs and no lone pair, so the F–B–F angles are 120° in one plane. Pyramidal would need a lone pair, as in NH₃.

questions.s: The hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethene, C₂H₄, is
questions.e: Each carbon forms three σ bonds (two C–H and one C–C), so three sp² orbitals are used, and the remaining p orbital forms the π bond. sp is found in ethyne.

questions.s: Which of the following molecules can form hydrogen bonds with other molecules of its own kind?
questions.e: Hydrogen bonding needs hydrogen attached to a small, highly electronegative atom (N, O or F). Methanol has an O–H group, but the other three have only C–H or C–Cl bonds.

questions.s: Which of the following molecules has polar bonds but is non-polar overall?
questions.e: The four C–Cl dipoles in the tetrahedral CCl₄ cancel each other. In CHCl₃ one bond is different, and NH₃ and H₂O are not symmetrical.

questions.s: The numbers of σ and π bonds in a molecule of ethyne, HC≡CH, are
questions.e: There are two C–H σ bonds and the triple bond contains one σ and two π, giving 3 σ and 2 π. A triple bond is not three σ bonds.

questions.s: Water boils at a much higher temperature than hydrogen sulphide mainly because water molecules
o: form hydrogen bonds with one another
questions.e: Hydrogen bonding between H₂O molecules needs extra energy to break, though H₂S is heavier. Boiling does not break the covalent bonds inside the molecules.

questions.s: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the expression for Kc is
questions.e: Products are in the numerator and reactants in the denominator, each raised to its coefficient. The inverted expression is the Kc for the reverse reaction.

questions.s: Increasing the pressure on the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at constant temperature
o: shifts the equilibrium to the left
has no effect on the position
shifts the equilibrium to the right
questions.e: Four moles of gas on the left become two on the right, so higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles. Kc changes only with temperature.

questions.s: For H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), the equilibrium concentrations are [H₂] = 0.10 M, [I₂] = 0.10 M and [HI] = 0.40 M. The value of Kc is
questions.e: Kc = [HI]²/([H₂][I₂]) = 0.16/0.01 = 16. 4 forgets to square [HI], and 0.0625 is the inverse.

questions.s: For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), the equilibrium concentrations are [N₂O₄] = 0.080 mol dm⁻³ and [NO₂] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³. Kc is
questions.e: Kc = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄] = (0.020)²/0.080 = 5.0 × 10⁻³, and since two moles of product come from one of reactant the unit is mol dm⁻³. Option 2.5 × 10⁻¹ is the inverted-ratio mistake of 0.020/0.080.

questions.s: The pH of a 0.01 M solution of hydrochloric acid is
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid, so [H⁺] = 0.01 = 10⁻² M and pH = 2. 12 would be the pH of a 0.01 M NaOH solution.

questions.s: The pH of a 0.001 M solution of sodium hydroxide at 25 °C is
questions.e: [OH⁻] = 10⁻³, so pOH = 3 and pH = 14 − 3 = 11. A pH of 3 would be that of 0.001 M acid.

questions.s: A solution has a pH of 3.7. Its hydrogen ion concentration is approximately
questions.e: [H⁺] = 10⁻³·⁷ = 10⁻⁴ × 10⁰·³ = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ M. 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ M corresponds to pH 3.3.

questions.s: Acetic acid has Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵. The pH of a 0.10 M solution is about
questions.e: For a weak acid [H⁺] = √(Ka × C) = √(1.8 × 10⁻⁶) = 1.34 × 10⁻³ M, so pH = 2.87. pH 1.00 would be a strong acid and 4.74 is the pKa.

questions.s: Which mixture is a buffer solution?
questions.e: A buffer needs a weak acid with its conjugate base (or a weak base with its conjugate acid). HCl and HNO₃ are strong acids, and NaOH is a strong base.

questions.s: For AgCl, Ksp = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol² dm⁻⁶ at 25 °C. The solubility of AgCl in pure water is about
questions.e: For a 1 : 1 salt Ksp = s², so s = √(1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰) = 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ M. The Ksp itself is not the solubility.

questions.s: Adding a catalyst to a reaction at equilibrium
o: does not change the value of Kc
shifts the equilibrium to the products
questions.e: A catalyst speeds up the forward and the reverse reactions equally, so the same equilibrium is reached sooner. Only a change of temperature alters Kc.

questions.s: For 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), the relation between Kp and Kc is
questions.e: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn, where Δn = 2 − 3 = −1. Kp = Kc only when Δn = 0.

questions.s: The unit of the rate constant for a first-order reaction is
questions.e: Rate = k[A] has units of mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹, so k must be in s⁻¹. The second option is the unit of the rate and the third is not a rate-constant unit at all.

questions.s: The rate of a reaction is given by rate = k[A]²[B]. If [A] is doubled and [B] is unchanged, the rate becomes
questions.e: Rate ∝ [A]², so doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 2² = 4. Twice would hold for a first-order dependence.

questions.s: For a first-order reaction, the half-life
o: is directly proportional to the initial concentration
is independent of the initial concentration
is inversely proportional to the initial concentration
decreases steadily as the reaction proceeds
questions.e: t½ = 0.693/k is a constant. A half-life proportional to the initial concentration is the behaviour of a zero-order reaction.

questions.s: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0231 min⁻¹. Its half-life is
questions.e: t½ = 0.693/k = 0.693/0.0231 = 30 min. 3.0 min is a power-of-ten slip.

questions.s: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction because it
o: provides a path with a lower activation energy
increases the energy released by the reaction
raises the temperature of the system
increases the equilibrium yield of the product
questions.e: A lower activation energy means a larger fraction of molecules can react at the same temperature. The enthalpy change and the equilibrium position stay the same.

questions.s: The rate of a reaction doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. If a reaction takes 40 minutes at 30 °C, the time taken at 60 °C is
questions.e: A 30 °C rise gives 2³ = 8 times the rate, so the time is 40/8 = 5 minutes. 13.3 minutes divides by 3 instead of 8.

questions.s: The increase in reaction rate on raising the temperature is mainly because
o: a larger fraction of molecules has energy of at least Ea
the molecules collide with a larger area
questions.e: The activation energy of a reaction is unchanged by temperature, but more molecules exceed it. The rise in collision frequency alone is far too small to explain the effect.

questions.s: For an exothermic reaction, the enthalpy change ΔH is
questions.e: Heat is released to the surroundings, so the enthalpy of the system falls and ΔH < 0. A positive ΔH describes an endothermic reaction.

questions.s: Given C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −393.5 kJ and CO(g) + ½O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −283.0 kJ, the enthalpy change of C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g) is
questions.e: Subtract the second equation from the first: −393.5 − (−283.0) = −110.5 kJ. Adding the two values gives −676.5 kJ, which does not represent the target reaction.

questions.s: The heat needed to raise the temperature of 200 g of water from 20 °C to 45 °C is (specific heat capacity 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.e: q = mcΔT = 200 × 4.18 × 25 = 20,900 J. 37,620 J would use the final temperature 45 instead of the change, giving 200 × 4.18 × 45.

questions.s: The enthalpy of combustion of methane is −890 kJ mol⁻¹. The heat released on burning 8 g of methane (CH₄ = 16 g/mol) is
questions.e: 8 g is 0.5 mol, so the heat is 0.5 × 890 = 445 kJ. 890 kJ is for a full mole.

questions.s: Which of the following has a standard enthalpy of formation equal to zero?
questions.e: An element in its most stable form at 298 K and 1 atm has ΔHf° = 0, and bromine is a liquid under these conditions. Gaseous bromine is not the standard state, so its ΔHf° is not zero.

questions.s: A reaction has ΔH = +40 kJ and ΔS = +100 J K⁻¹. It becomes spontaneous at temperatures above
questions.e: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS < 0 when T > ΔH/ΔS = 40,000/100 = 400 K, with ΔH converted to joules. Forgetting the conversion gives 0.4 K.

questions.s: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. The change in its internal energy is
questions.e: ΔU = q + w = 500 + (−200) = +300 J, since work done by the gas is negative. Adding the two magnitudes would give +700 J.

questions.s: The oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄ is
questions.e: K is +1 and four oxygens give −8, so Mn must be +7 for a neutral compound. +6 is the state in K₂MnO₄.

questions.s: The oxidation number of chromium in potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇, is
questions.e: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0 gives 2x = 12, so x = +6. +12 is the total for both chromium atoms.

questions.s: Standard electrode potentials are Zn²⁺/Zn = −0.76 V and Cu²⁺/Cu = +0.34 V. The standard e.m.f. of the Zn–Cu cell is
questions.e: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V, with copper as the cathode. 0.42 V comes from adding the two electrode potentials instead of subtracting them.

questions.s: The mass of copper deposited when a current of 2 A passes through copper(II) sulphate solution for 965 s is (Cu = 63.5, F = 96,500 C/mol)
questions.e: Q = 2 × 965 = 1,930 C = 0.02 mol of electrons, and Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu gives 0.01 mol = 0.635 g. 1.27 g forgets that two electrons are needed per atom.

questions.s: During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride, the gas liberated at the cathode is
questions.e: Water is reduced more easily than Na⁺, so H₂ forms at the cathode and Cl₂ at the anode. Sodium is obtained only from molten NaCl.

questions.s: In a galvanic cell, the electrons flow in the external circuit
o: from the cathode to the anode
from the positive to the negative electrode
from the anode to the cathode
questions.e: Oxidation at the anode releases electrons, which travel through the wire to the cathode. The salt bridge carries ions only.

questions.s: Which of the following metals will NOT displace copper from copper(II) sulphate solution?
questions.e: A metal displaces copper only if it is above copper in the electrochemical series (a more negative E°). Silver (E° = +0.80 V) lies below copper.

questions.s: The molarity of a solution containing 4.0 g of NaOH (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1) in 500 cm³ of solution is
questions.e: n = 4.0/40 = 0.10 mol, and the volume is 0.5 dm³, so the molarity is 0.20 M. 0.1 M forgets to convert 500 cm³ to 0.5 dm³.

questions.s: The molality of a solution of 9 g of glucose (180 g/mol) in 500 g of water is
questions.e: n = 9/180 = 0.05 mol and the solvent is 0.5 kg, so m = 0.05/0.5 = 0.1 mol kg⁻¹. 0.05 m forgets to divide by the mass in kilograms.

questions.s: Taking Kb for water as 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹, a 0.5 molal solution of glucose boils at about
questions.e: ΔTb = Kb × m = 0.52 × 0.5 = 0.26 K, so the boiling point is 100.26 °C. 99.74 °C subtracts the elevation, and 100.52 °C forgets the molality.

questions.s: Taking Kf for water as 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹, the freezing point of a solution of 6 g of urea (60 g/mol) in 100 g of water is
questions.e: m = (6/60)/0.100 = 1.0 mol kg⁻¹, so ΔTf = 1.86 K and the solution freezes at −1.86 °C. The mass of solvent must be taken in kilograms.

questions.s: With R = 0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, the osmotic pressure of a 0.10 M glucose solution at 27 °C is about
questions.e: π = CRT = 0.10 × 0.0821 × 300 = 2.46 atm, using T in kelvin. 25 atm is a power-of-ten error.

questions.s: The vapour pressure of pure solvent is 100 mmHg. A solution in which the mole fraction of the solvent is 0.8 has a vapour pressure of (ideal behaviour)
questions.e: By Raoult's law P = x × P° = 0.8 × 100 = 80 mmHg. 20 mmHg uses the mole fraction of the solute.

questions.s: A 0.10 molal solution of NaCl is nearly completely dissociated. Using Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹, its freezing-point depression is about
questions.e: NaCl gives two ions, so the van't Hoff factor i ≈ 2 and ΔTf = 2 × 1.86 × 0.10 = 0.372 K. 0.19 K ignores dissociation.

questions.s: According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid at constant temperature is
o: directly proportional to the pressure of the gas
inversely proportional to the pressure of the gas
independent of the pressure of the gas
directly proportional to the square of the pressure
questions.e: Higher pressure forces more gas into solution, as in a sealed soda bottle. Inverse proportionality would mean the gas escapes as pressure rises.

questions.s: The shape of the sulphur hexafluoride molecule, SF₆, is
questions.e: Sulphur has six bond pairs and no lone pairs, which are directed to the corners of an octahedron. Trigonal bipyramidal is the shape of PCl₅ with five pairs.

questions.s: The nitrogen atom in ammonia is hybridised as
questions.e: Nitrogen has three bond pairs and one lone pair, four regions in total, so four sp³ orbitals are used. sp² would give a trigonal planar arrangement.

questions.s: Treating both stages of ionisation as complete, the pH of a 0.05 M solution of sulphuric acid is
questions.e: Each H₂SO₄ gives two H⁺, so [H⁺] = 0.10 M and pH = 1. 1.3 is the pH of 0.05 M of a monobasic strong acid.

questions.s: The unit of the rate constant of a zero-order reaction is
questions.e: For rate = k, the constant has the units of rate itself, mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. The unit s⁻¹ belongs to a first-order constant.

questions.s: The enthalpy change when one mole of water is formed from H⁺ and OH⁻ in the neutralisation of a strong acid by a strong base is about
questions.e: The net change is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O, which is exothermic by about 57 kJ mol⁻¹ for any strong acid and base. −286 kJ is the enthalpy of formation of liquid water.

questions.s: The time needed to pass 0.10 mol of electrons through a cell using a steady current of 2.0 A is (F = 96,500 C/mol)
questions.e: Q = 0.10 × 96,500 = 9,650 C, and t = Q/I = 9,650/2.0 = 4,825 s. 9,650 s forgets to divide by the current.

questions.s: A solution contains 2 mol of substance A and 3 mol of substance B. The mole fraction of A is
questions.e: x(A) = 2/(2 + 3) = 0.4. 0.67 is the ratio 2/3, which is not a mole fraction.

questions.s: The forward reaction of an equilibrium is exothermic. Raising the temperature
o: shifts the equilibrium to the right and raises Kc
shifts the equilibrium to the left and lowers Kc
shifts the equilibrium to the left without changing Kc
has no effect on the equilibrium
questions.e: By Le Chatelier's principle the system absorbs heat by favouring the endothermic reverse reaction, and Kc falls.

questions.s: A reaction is spontaneous at constant temperature and pressure when
questions.e: A negative free-energy change ΔG = ΔH − TΔS marks a spontaneous process. A negative ΔH alone is not enough, since TΔS also matters.

questions.s: According to molecular orbital theory, the bond order of the oxygen molecule O₂ is
questions.e: O₂ has 8 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons, so the bond order is (8 − 4)/2 = 2. Bond order 3 belongs to N₂, and 2.5 to O₂⁺.

questions.s: Across the third period from sodium to argon, the first ionisation energy generally
questions.e: Nuclear charge rises while the shielding stays the same, so electrons are held more tightly. Decreasing is the trend down a group.

questions.s: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.e: Fluorine is the smallest halogen with the highest effective nuclear attraction, and has a Pauling value of 4.0. Chlorine is lower because its atom is larger.

questions.s: Which of the following atoms has the largest atomic radius?
questions.e: These elements are in the same period, and the radius decreases from left to right as the nuclear charge increases. Sodium is on the far left.

questions.s: Which element has the highest first ionisation energy?
questions.e: Helium's two electrons are in the first shell, very close to a nucleus of charge +2 with no shielding. Neon is lower because its outer electrons are farther away.

questions.s: Among the isoelectronic ions O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺ and Mg²⁺, the one with the largest radius is
questions.e: All have ten electrons, so the ion with the fewest protons (8) has the weakest pull on them and the largest radius. Mg²⁺ has 12 protons and is the smallest.

questions.s: Among the halogens, the element with the most negative electron affinity (largest energy released on gaining an electron) is
questions.e: Fluorine is so small that the added electron is strongly repelled by the electrons already present, so chlorine releases more energy. The values then fall from chlorine to iodine.

questions.s: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
questions.e: Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases, forming salts with each. Na₂O and MgO are basic, and SO₃ is acidic.

questions.s: An element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴. It belongs to group
questions.e: The outer shell holds 2 + 4 = 6 electrons, so it is in group 16 (the oxygen family), and the element is sulphur. Group 14 would have four outer electrons.

questions.s: The number of elements in the third period of the periodic table is
questions.e: The third period fills the 3s and 3p subshells, 2 + 6 = 8 elements, from sodium to argon. 18 elements are in periods 4 and 5.

questions.s: Lithium shows a diagonal relationship with
questions.e: Li (group 1, period 2) and Mg (group 2, period 3) have similar charge density and show similar behaviour, for example both form nitrides. Beryllium is the one that pairs with aluminium.

questions.s: Going down group 1 from lithium to caesium, the reaction of the metals with water becomes more vigorous because
o: the atoms become smaller in size
the outer electron is lost more easily
questions.e: The atomic radius grows and the outer electron is farther from the nucleus, so the ionisation energy falls and it is lost more readily. The atoms do not get smaller going down a group.

questions.s: The only non-metallic element that is a liquid at room temperature is
questions.e: Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature, while chlorine is a gas and iodine and sulphur are solids. Mercury is the liquid metal.

questions.s: Which of the following xenon compounds is known?
questions.e: Xenon's large size and low ionisation energy let it bond with fluorine, giving XeF₂, XeF₄ and XeF₆. Helium and argon form no stable compounds under ordinary conditions.

questions.s: When sodium is added to water, the products are
questions.e: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Oxygen is never a product, because the metal reduces water.

questions.s: The main product when sodium burns in excess air or oxygen is
questions.e: Sodium forms the peroxide when it burns in a good supply of oxygen. The normal oxide Na₂O forms in limited oxygen, while lithium gives the oxide.

questions.s: The chemical formula of washing soda is
questions.e: Washing soda is the decahydrate of sodium carbonate. Na₂CO₃ alone is soda ash, and NaHCO₃ is baking soda.

questions.s: The formula of plaster of Paris is
questions.e: Heating gypsum, CaSO₄·2H₂O, at about 120 °C drives off three-quarters of its water and leaves the hemihydrate. Gypsum itself has two molecules of water.

questions.s: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky because it forms
questions.e: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, and the insoluble calcium carbonate gives the milky look. With excess CO₂ the cloudiness clears as Ca(HCO₃)₂ dissolves.

questions.s: Temporary hardness of water, which is removed by boiling, is caused by the presence of
questions.e: On boiling, Ca(HCO₃)₂ decomposes to insoluble CaCO₃, CO₂ and water. Sulphates and chlorides cause permanent hardness.

questions.s: In the Solvay process, the compound that separates out when carbon dioxide is passed through ammoniated brine is
questions.e: NaCl + NH₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → NaHCO₃ + NH₄Cl, and NaHCO₃ is the least soluble so it precipitates. It is then heated to give sodium carbonate.

questions.s: When magnesium burns in air, the products are mainly
questions.e: Magnesium burns brightly to give the oxide, and it is hot enough to combine a little with nitrogen to form Mg₃N₂. The product MgO alone ignores this side reaction.

questions.s: The oxidation number of nitrogen in nitric acid, HNO₃, is
questions.e: +1 + x + 3(−2) = 0 gives x = +5. The state −3 is that of nitrogen in ammonia.

questions.s: Ammonia is prepared in the laboratory by heating ammonium chloride with
questions.e: 2NH₄Cl + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O + 2NH₃. An acid would react with the ammonia produced.

questions.s: The ozone layer in the stratosphere protects life on Earth by absorbing
questions.e: Ozone absorbs harmful UV-B and UV-C. The warmth we feel from the Sun is mainly infrared, which passes through.

questions.s: Acid rain is caused mainly by the dissolving in rain water of
questions.e: SO₂ and NOₓ form sulphurous, sulphuric and nitric acids in the atmosphere. CO₂ makes rain only slightly acidic.

questions.s: Concentrated sulphuric acid chars sugar because it acts as a
questions.e: The acid removes hydrogen and oxygen from the sugar as water, leaving black carbon. It does this by pulling out the elements of water, not by acting as a base.

questions.s: When chlorine gas is passed through a solution of potassium bromide, the colour changes to orange-brown because
questions.e: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂, because chlorine is the stronger oxidising agent. The reverse reaction does not occur.

questions.s: Bleaching powder is manufactured by passing chlorine over
questions.e: Cl₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O. Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, while quicklime is CaO.

questions.s: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.e: Acid strength of the oxyacids of one element rises with the number of oxygen atoms and the oxidation state of chlorine, +7 here. Perchloric acid is the strongest of the four.

questions.s: Among the hydrogen halides, the one with the highest boiling point is
questions.e: Hydrogen bonding between HF molecules raises its boiling point above that of HCl. The other three increase in boiling point with molar mass but stay lower.

questions.s: Silicon dioxide has a very high melting point because it
o: contains Si⁴⁺ and O²⁻ ions in a lattice
has strong hydrogen bonds between layers
questions.e: Every silicon atom is joined to four oxygen atoms and each oxygen to two silicon atoms, all by covalent bonds. This differs from CO₂, which has simple molecules.

questions.s: Which of the following is NOT a transition element?
questions.e: Aluminium is a p-block element in Group 13. Iron, copper and manganese are d-block transition elements with partly filled d subshells in common ions.

questions.s: The colour of the hydrated copper(II) ion in aqueous solution is
questions.e: [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ absorbs in the red-orange region and appears blue. Zn²⁺ solutions are colourless.

questions.s: The number of unpaired electrons in the Fe³⁺ ion (Z = 26) is
questions.e: Fe³⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁵ with one electron in each of the five d orbitals. Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) has four unpaired electrons.

questions.s: The number of unpaired electrons in the Cr³⁺ ion (Z = 24) is
questions.e: Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹, and losing three electrons leaves 3d³ with three unpaired electrons, according to Hund's rule. 6 is the unpaired-electron count of the neutral atom.

questions.s: The oxidation state of iron in the complex ion [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is
questions.e: Each CN⁻ carries −1, so six give −6 and x − 6 = −4 gives x = +2. +3 is the state of iron in [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻.

questions.s: The coordination number of copper in the complex ion [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ is
questions.e: The coordination number is the number of ligand donor atoms attached to the metal, here four NH₃ molecules. The charge 2+ is not the coordination number.

questions.s: Brass is an alloy of
questions.e: Brass is copper with zinc, and bronze is copper with tin. Steel is iron with carbon.

questions.s: When acidified potassium dichromate is reduced, its colour changes from
questions.e: Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) is reduced to Cr³⁺ (green), as in the breathalyser test. The reverse is oxidation.

questions.s: Which of the following transition elements shows oxidation states from +2 up to +7 in its compounds?
questions.e: Manganese forms Mn²⁺, MnO₂ (+4), MnO₄²⁻ (+6) and MnO₄⁻ (+7) among others. Scandium shows only +3 and zinc only +2.

questions.s: The catalyst used in the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia is
questions.e: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is catalysed by iron with promoters. V₂O₅ is for the contact process and platinum for oxidising ammonia.

questions.s: The catalyst used in the contact process for sulphuric acid is
questions.e: V₂O₅ catalyses 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ at about 450 °C. Iron is for the Haber process.

questions.s: In the Ostwald process, ammonia is oxidised over a platinum catalyst to give
questions.e: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O, and the NO is then oxidised to NO₂ and absorbed in water to give nitric acid. NO₂ and HNO₃ form in later stages.

questions.s: In the contact process, sulphur trioxide is absorbed in concentrated sulphuric acid, not in water, because
o: water reacts too slowly with the SO₃ gas
the acid acts as a catalyst for absorption
water would give a fine acid mist
SO₃ is completely insoluble in water
questions.e: SO₃ reacts violently with water, producing a mist of sulphuric acid that is difficult to collect. Dissolving it in the acid gives oleum, which is then diluted.

questions.s: The electrolysis of brine in a diaphragm cell gives
o: sodium at the cathode and chlorine at the anode
Cl₂ at the anode, H₂ at the cathode and NaOH solution
oxygen at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode
chlorine at the cathode and hydrogen at the anode
questions.e: Cl⁻ is oxidised at the anode, water is reduced at the cathode to H₂ and OH⁻, and the Na⁺ left in solution forms NaOH. Sodium metal is obtained only from molten NaCl.

questions.s: Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to alumina in the electrolytic extraction of aluminium in order to
o: raise the melting point of the molten mixture
oxidise the aluminium that is formed
prevent oxygen forming at the anode
lower the melting point and aid conduction
questions.e: Pure Al₂O₃ melts above 2,000 °C, but in molten cryolite the electrolysis can run near 950 °C. This saves a great deal of energy.

questions.s: The main reducing agent in the iron blast furnace is
questions.e: Carbon burns to CO₂, which reacts with more coke to give CO, and CO reduces Fe₂O₃ to iron. CO₂ is a product of the reduction, not a reducing agent.

questions.s: In the blast furnace, limestone is added to
o: reduce the iron ore to metal
raise the carbon content of the iron
act as a fuel for the furnace
questions.e: CaCO₃ decomposes to CaO, which combines with SiO₂ to form molten CaSiO₃ that floats on the iron. It does not act as a reducing agent or a fuel.

questions.s: The percentage of nitrogen by mass in urea, CO(NH₂)₂ (C = 12, O = 16, N = 14, H = 1), is
questions.e: M = 12 + 16 + 2(14 + 2) = 60, and N is 28/60 = 46.7 %. 23.3 % counts only one nitrogen atom.

questions.s: The two main raw materials used in the manufacture of Portland cement are
questions.e: Limestone provides calcium and clay provides silica, alumina and iron oxide. The mixture is heated to form clinker, and a little gypsum is added later.

questions.s: The raw materials used in making ordinary glass are
questions.e: Silica (sand) forms the network, soda ash lowers the melting point and limestone makes the glass durable.

questions.s: Calcium compounds give which colour to a Bunsen flame?
questions.e: Calcium gives a brick-red flame. Golden yellow is sodium, lilac is potassium and apple green is barium.

questions.s: The strongest oxidising agent among the halogens is
questions.e: Fluorine has the highest electrode potential, so it takes electrons most readily and can oxidise the other halide ions.

questions.s: When lithium is left in nitrogen gas at room temperature, it forms
questions.e: Lithium is the only alkali metal that combines directly with nitrogen at ordinary temperatures, giving Li₃N. The other options are not formed.

questions.s: The percentage of nitrogen by mass in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃ (N = 14, H = 1, O = 16), is
questions.e: M = 14 + 4 + 14 + 48 = 80, and 28/80 = 35.0 %. 46.7 % is the nitrogen content of urea.

questions.s: When a glass rod dipped in concentrated hydrochloric acid is held near ammonia gas, the observation is
questions.e: NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl, and the solid ammonium chloride forms as tiny particles, which look like white smoke.

questions.s: The first ionisation energy of beryllium is greater than that of magnesium mainly because in beryllium
o: the outer electron is closer to the nucleus
questions.e: Both are in group 2, but beryllium's outer electron is in the second shell, nearer the nucleus and less shielded. Magnesium has the larger nuclear charge, but it is outweighed by the extra shell.

questions.s: Most compounds of transition metals are coloured because
o: they all contain unpaired s electrons
their d electrons jump between split d levels
they contain free ions in the lattice
questions.e: The d orbitals split in energy in a compound, and visible light promotes an electron between them (d–d transition). The colour seen is the light not absorbed.

questions.s: The oxidation number of sulphur in sulphur dioxide, SO₂, is
questions.e: x + 2(−2) = 0 gives x = +4. +6 is the state in SO₃.

questions.s: Sodium metal is stored under kerosene because it
o: is a radioactive element in nature
reacts rapidly with air and moisture
is a liquid at room temperature
dissolves into the water vapour present
questions.e: Sodium is oxidised quickly in air and reacts vigorously with water, so it is kept out of contact with both.

questions.s: The general formula of the alkane series is
questions.e: Alkanes are saturated, with each carbon bonded to as many hydrogens as possible. CₙH₂ₙ is the formula of alkenes and CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ of alkynes.

questions.s: The number of structural isomers of pentane, C₅H₁₂, is
questions.e: They are pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane. Butane, C₄H₁₀, has two isomers.

questions.s: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ is
questions.e: The longest chain has four carbons with a methyl group on carbon 2 when numbered from the nearer end. Numbering from the other end would wrongly give 3-methylbutane.

questions.s: The main product of the addition of hydrogen bromide to propene is
questions.e: By Markovnikov's rule hydrogen adds to the carbon with more hydrogens, so bromine goes to the middle carbon, which gives the more stable secondary carbocation.

questions.s: Which reagent is used to distinguish an alkene from an alkane at room temperature?
questions.e: An alkene adds bromine and decolourises the orange-brown solution quickly, while an alkane does not react in the dark.

questions.s: Ethene is prepared in the laboratory by heating ethanol with
questions.e: Concentrated H₂SO₄ dehydrates the alcohol: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O. Dichromate would oxidise ethanol instead.

questions.s: The gas formed when calcium carbide reacts with water is
questions.e: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂. The carbide ion C₂²⁻ has a triple bond and gives acetylene (ethyne).

questions.s: Which of the following gives a precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate solution?
questions.e: Terminal alkynes have an acidic hydrogen on the sp carbon and form a silver acetylide precipitate. Alkenes and alkanes have no such hydrogen.

questions.s: All the carbon–carbon bonds in a benzene molecule are
o: all double bonds of length 134 pm
all single bonds of length 154 pm
equal in length, between single and double
questions.e: The π electrons are delocalised over the ring, so all six bonds are equal (about 140 pm). The Kekulé structure with alternate bonds does not describe this.

questions.s: The electrophile in the nitration of benzene with a mixture of concentrated nitric and sulphuric acids is
questions.e: Sulphuric acid protonates HNO₃, which then loses water to form the nitronium ion NO₂⁺. The nitrate ion is a negative species and cannot attack the ring.

questions.s: The reaction of methane with chlorine in ultraviolet light is classified as
questions.e: UV light splits Cl₂ into chlorine atoms, which start a radical chain that replaces H by Cl. Methane has no π bond, so addition is impossible.

questions.s: Bromomethane heated with sodium metal in dry ether gives mainly
questions.e: This is the Wurtz reaction: 2CH₃Br + 2Na → C₂H₆ + 2NaBr. The new bond joins two methyl groups.

questions.s: The total number of σ bonds in a molecule of propane, C₃H₈, is
questions.e: There are 2 C–C bonds and 8 C–H bonds, all σ. Eight is only the number of C–H bonds.

questions.s: The volume of oxygen needed for the complete combustion of 2 dm³ of ethane, with all volumes at the same temperature and pressure, is
questions.e: C₂H₆ + 3½O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O, so 1 volume needs 3.5 volumes of O₂, and 2 × 3.5 = 7 dm³. 3.5 dm³ is the figure for one volume of ethane.

questions.s: The number of moles of hydrogen that add to one mole of ethyne to give ethane is
questions.e: HC≡CH + H₂ → H₂C=CH₂ and then + H₂ → CH₃CH₃, so two moles in all. One mole stops at ethene.

questions.s: But-2-ene shows cis–trans isomerism because
o: it has a chiral carbon atom in the chain
it contains a triple bond in the chain
rotation about the C=C bond is restricted
it has two different functional groups present
questions.e: Each carbon of the double bond carries two different groups, and the π bond stops them rotating. But-1-ene has two H atoms on one of the carbons, so it does not show this.

questions.s: The IUPAC name of CH₃COCH₃ is
questions.e: The carbonyl group is within the chain, making it a ketone with three carbons. Propanal would have the C=O at the end of the chain.

questions.s: The functional group present in carboxylic acids is
questions.e: A carboxylic acid has a carbonyl and a hydroxyl on the same carbon. –CHO is an aldehyde and –COO– is an ester.

questions.s: Which of the following is a secondary alcohol?
questions.e: In a secondary alcohol the carbon bearing the –OH group is attached to two other carbons. Propan-1-ol is primary and 2-methylpropan-2-ol is tertiary.

questions.s: Ethanol heated under reflux with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI) is oxidised to
questions.e: A primary alcohol is oxidised first to the aldehyde and then to the carboxylic acid, and reflux ensures complete oxidation. Ethanal is obtained only if it is distilled off as it forms.

questions.s: Which alcohol is NOT oxidised by acidified potassium dichromate?
questions.e: A tertiary alcohol has no hydrogen on the carbon carrying the –OH group, so it cannot be oxidised without breaking the carbon skeleton.

questions.s: In the Lucas test, the alcohol that reacts fastest with zinc chloride in concentrated hydrochloric acid, becoming cloudy, is
questions.e: The tertiary alcohol forms the most stable carbocation and so reacts almost at once. A primary alcohol shows no cloudiness at room temperature.

questions.s: Which of the following compounds gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
questions.e: Aldehydes are oxidised to carboxylate ions while Ag⁺ is reduced to silver. Ketones such as propanone do not react.

questions.s: The ester formed when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid is
questions.e: The alcohol provides the ethyl part and the acid the ethanoate part, giving CH₃COOC₂H₅ and water. Ethyl methanoate would come from methanoic acid.

questions.s: The alkaline hydrolysis of an ester, such as the reaction of a fat with sodium hydroxide, is called
questions.e: The ester splits into an alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid, which is soap in the case of fats. Esterification is the reverse, acid-catalysed formation.

questions.s: Phenol is acidic enough to react with aqueous
questions.e: Phenol (pKa about 10) is a weak acid but reacts with a strong base to form sodium phenoxide. It is too weak to release CO₂ from a hydrogencarbonate.

questions.s: Methylamine, CH₃NH₂, is a weak base because
o: it contains an –OH group that ionises
nitrogen has a lone pair that accepts a proton
it has a double bond to the nitrogen atom
it releases hydroxide ions by itself directly
questions.e: The nitrogen lone pair binds H⁺ to form CH₃NH₃⁺. It contains no –OH group of its own; hydroxide arises from water.

questions.s: Which of the following gives a yellow precipitate when warmed with iodine and sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.e: The iodoform test needs a CH₃CO– group, or CH₃CH(OH)– that is oxidised to one. Propanone has it, but propan-1-ol and methanol do not.

questions.s: A functional isomer of ethanol is
questions.e: Both have the molecular formula C₂H₆O, but methoxymethane (CH₃OCH₃) is an ether. Ethoxyethane is C₄H₁₀O.

questions.s: Ethanal is reduced to ethanol by
questions.e: NaBH₄ and LiAlH₄ add hydride to the carbonyl carbon, giving an alcohol. Dichromate and Tollens' reagent are oxidising agents.

questions.s: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CHO is
questions.e: There are three carbons and the aldehyde group is at the end, so it is propanal. Ethanal has only two.

questions.s: The percentage of carbon by mass in ethanol, C₂H₅OH (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16), is
questions.e: M = 46, and carbon contributes 24, so 24/46 × 100 = 52.2 %. 26.1 % counts only one carbon.

questions.s: The reaction of bromoethane with aqueous potassium hydroxide to give ethanol is
questions.e: The OH⁻ nucleophile replaces the bromide ion on the carbon atom. In an elimination, a double bond would form.

questions.s: Bromoethane heated with an alcoholic solution of potassium hydroxide gives mainly
questions.e: Under alcoholic conditions the hydroxide acts as a base and removes HBr from the molecule. In aqueous solution the substitution product ethanol forms.

questions.s: An SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon atom results in
questions.e: The nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group in a single step, so the configuration is inverted. A racemic mixture is typical of SN1.

questions.s: The correct order of stability of carbocations is
questions.e: Alkyl groups donate electrons by the inductive effect and hyperconjugation, spreading out the positive charge. More alkyl groups mean greater stability.

questions.s: Which of the following species can act as an electrophile?
questions.e: Boron in BF₃ has an incomplete octet and accepts a lone pair. The other three have lone pairs and are nucleophiles.

questions.s: Benzene reacts with chloromethane in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride to give
questions.e: This is a Friedel–Crafts alkylation, in which AlCl₃ generates the CH₃⁺ electrophile. Chlorobenzene would form with Cl₂ and iron(III) chloride.

questions.s: In homolytic fission of a covalent bond
o: both electrons go to the more electronegative atom, forming ions
the bond is always broken by a nucleophile
each atom takes one electron, forming free radicals
a carbocation is always formed as the intermediate
questions.e: Homolytic fission gives two neutral species with unpaired electrons, favoured by heat or light. Heterolytic fission gives ions.

questions.s: The hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane by water follows the SN1 mechanism mainly because
o: a stable tertiary carbocation can form
the carbon atom is not hindered
the bromide ion is a poor leaving group
the molecule has a chiral carbon
questions.e: The tertiary carbocation is stable, and three bulky groups hinder a backside attack. Bromide is actually a good leaving group, and the molecule is not chiral.

questions.s: The reaction of ethene with bromine in an inert solvent is
questions.e: The electron-rich double bond polarises the Br–Br molecule and attacks it, forming 1,2-dibromoethane.

questions.s: The conversion of ethanol to ethene by heating with concentrated sulphuric acid is an example of
questions.e: A molecule of water is removed from adjacent carbons, creating a C=C bond. Addition would be the reverse reaction.

questions.s: Which of the following reacts fastest with hydroxide ions by the SN2 mechanism?
questions.e: SN2 needs backside access to the carbon, which is easiest when there are no alkyl groups on it. The rate falls as the carbon becomes more substituted.

questions.s: The formation of ethyl ethanoate from ethanoic acid and ethanol, with the loss of a molecule of water, is an example of a
questions.e: Two molecules combine with the loss of a small molecule, here H₂O. Neither molecule has an oxidation number change.

questions.s: The molecular formula of glucose is
questions.e: Glucose is a hexose with six carbons. C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ is the formula of sucrose and maltose.

questions.s: The hydrolysis of sucrose with dilute acid gives
questions.e: Sucrose is a disaccharide of α-glucose and β-fructose, joined through both anomeric carbons. Maltose gives two molecules of glucose.

questions.s: Cellulose is a polymer of
questions.e: β-Glucose units are linked in straight chains that pack together as fibres. α-Glucose units form starch and glycogen.

questions.s: In the formation of a peptide bond between two amino acids, the molecule eliminated is
questions.e: The –COOH of one amino acid reacts with the –NH₂ of the other to form –CONH– and H₂O.

questions.s: The alkaline hydrolysis of a fat or oil gives
questions.e: A fat is a triester of glycerol and long-chain fatty acids. Sodium hydroxide gives glycerol and the sodium salts of the acids, which are soaps.

questions.s: In a DNA double helix, adenine forms base pairs with
questions.e: A pairs with T through two hydrogen bonds, and G pairs with C through three. Uracil takes the place of thymine only in RNA.

questions.s: Maltose is a disaccharide made up of
questions.e: Hydrolysis of maltose gives two molecules of glucose. Glucose with fructose is sucrose, and with galactose it is lactose.

questions.s: Which of the following sugars does NOT give a positive test with Fehling's solution?
questions.e: In sucrose both anomeric carbons are tied up in the glycosidic bond, so there is no free aldehyde or ketone group. The other three have free carbonyl forms.

questions.s: Most enzymes stop working at high temperatures because
o: the enzyme is converted into a sugar
questions.e: Heat breaks the hydrogen bonds that hold the tertiary structure, so the active site loses its shape.

questions.s: The monomer of polythene (polyethylene) is
questions.e: Many ethene molecules add together through their double bonds to form poly(ethene).

questions.s: Poly(vinyl chloride), PVC, is made from the monomer
questions.e: The monomer is vinyl chloride, CH₂=CHCl, which has the double bond needed for addition polymerisation. Chloroethane is saturated.

questions.s: Nylon-6,6 is made from hexane-1,6-diamine and hexanedioic acid by
questions.e: The –NH₂ and –COOH groups link by amide bonds with the loss of water at each step.

questions.s: The monomer of Teflon is
questions.e: Teflon is poly(tetrafluoroethene), with a CF₂–CF₂ repeat unit, formed by addition polymerisation. Fluoroethene would give a polymer with fewer fluorine atoms.

questions.s: Natural rubber is a polymer of
questions.e: The monomer is isoprene, with a methyl group on carbon 2. Buta-1,3-diene is the monomer of the synthetic polybutadiene.

questions.s: Vulcanisation of natural rubber involves heating it with
o: oxygen, which breaks the long chains
chlorine, which makes it more flexible
hydrogen, which saturates the double bonds
questions.e: Sulphur bridges join neighbouring chains, making the rubber harder, stronger and more elastic.

questions.s: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.e: Bakelite has a highly cross-linked network and cannot be softened again once set. Polythene, PVC and polystyrene soften on heating.

questions.s: The mass of carbon dioxide formed by the complete combustion of 0.1 mol of propane, C₃H₈ (C = 12, O = 16), is
questions.e: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O, so 0.1 mol gives 0.3 mol of CO₂ = 0.3 × 44 = 13.2 g. 4.4 g would be for one carbon per molecule.

questions.s: 60 g of ethanoic acid is heated with excess ethanol, and the yield of ethyl ethanoate (88 g/mol) is 70 %. The mass of ester obtained is
questions.e: 60 g of CH₃COOH (60 g/mol) is 1.0 mol, so the theoretical yield is 88 g and 70 % of this is 61.6 g. 88 g is the theoretical yield.

questions.s: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃ is
questions.e: The longest chain has four carbons, and numbering from the end nearer to –OH gives position 2.

questions.s: The hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethyne is
questions.e: Each carbon forms two σ bonds and two π bonds, so only two hybrid orbitals are needed and the carbon is linear.

questions.s: Which of the following gives a red precipitate on warming with Fehling's solution?
questions.e: Aliphatic aldehydes reduce Cu²⁺ to red copper(I) oxide. Ketones and alcohols give no change.

questions.s: A few drops of iodine solution turn which of the following blue-black?
questions.e: Iodine fits within the helical coil of starch (amylose) to give the blue-black colour. Cellulose is straight-chained and gives no such colour.

questions.s: The monomer of polystyrene is
questions.e: Polystyrene is made by addition polymerisation of styrene, C₆H₅CH=CH₂. Benzene has no side-chain double bond.

questions.s: Which of the following will decolourise cold, dilute, alkaline potassium manganate(VII)?
questions.e: The alkene is oxidised to a diol and the purple colour changes. Alkanes and benzene are unreactive towards cold dilute permanganate.

questions.s: At its isoelectric point, an amino acid exists mainly as
o: a neutral molecule with a free –COOH
questions.e: The proton of the –COOH moves to the –NH₂, giving ⁺H₃N–CHR–COO⁻, which has no net charge. It is not a molecule with a free acid group.

questions.s: The number of structural isomers of butane, C₄H₁₀, is
questions.e: They are butane and 2-methylpropane. A third would need a different formula.
